Artificial intelligence ( #AI ) has shown remarkable abilities to reason, problem solve, and control machines—but could tiny models of brain tissue grown in the lab do the same? Led by #BaskinEngineering Assistant Professor of Biomolecular Engineering Tal Sharf, a team of researchers at the UC Santa Cruz Genomics Institute , will explore this question with support from a $1.9 million National Science Foundation (NSF) grant. Their work will create an interactive system to test whether brain organoids can learn from experience, respond to feedback, and solve tasks in real time. “These organoid models provide an unprecedented opportunity to probe the emergence of human cognitive capacity – a property that defines what makes us human,” said Sharf, who is a member of the Braingeneers group. This research could drive new biomedical discoveries and lead to better therapies for disease. Co-investigators include Distinguished Professor of Biomolecular Engineering David Haussler, Associate Professor of Electrical and Computer Engineering Mircea Teodorescu , and research scientist at the Genomics Institute Mohammed Mostajo-Radji , and Hank Greely, Stanford Law Professor and Director of the Center for Law and the Biosciences. activity.title: Everyone dogs on refs, but it's such a thankless job. You have to be: - Supremely fit - Extremely cool under pressure - Okay with millions (if not billions) scrutinizing every single decision you make - Constantly accused of cheating - Able to manage some of the largest egos on the planet. On top of this, you may have to work a second job because even if you ref the World Cup Final you'll make less in a year than a new grad software engineer. Yes, refs often make nonsensical decisions. But it shouldn't be hard to have some empathy for them.

Do you know which commands your agents are running? Coding agents can now create files, install packages, run scripts, and modify entire projects. Yet, many junior devs approve commands they don't fully understand (including me!) That is why Lily Wu and I built Terminal Trails, a game that teaches essential shell commands through short, interactive levels. We built it for the Bruin Software Engineers fellowship so our members can use coding agents confidently and avoid the mistakes we made. Thank you to Professor Paul Eggert, Alexander Pak, Alexander An, and Mukund SK for playtesting it! Try it: https://lnkd.in/gzy6qtvr

It was an important week for me. After a tedious and dry 1st-half of the year, I got 3 offers this week. Google , Capital One and DoorDash . Each came with its own terms and conditions. I spent some time comparing the financial implications, future consequences and risks. Finally made a decision. Google was enticing, but I’m delighted to say I’m choosing DoorDash . Thank you to everyone who believed in me. Offer details: - Google: Keep Google AI Pro for $5.99/month after my free student year. - Capital One: $250 checking account bonus after qualifying direct deposits. - DoorDash: $0 delivery fees, and 10% off at Cheesecake Factory. It was an obvious choice.
